title: Unified Inference — Product overview, PRD, design, roadmap, pricing and release notes (v13)
author: Asha Patel
body:
Summary
This single-source product document summarizes the Unified Inference product (v13): the high-level product overview, the core PRD requirements we shipped, high-level design decisions, the roadmap and themes for the next two quarters, pricing and packaging notes, and the v13 release notes with rollout guidance. Intended audience: product, engineering, sales, customer success, and partner engineers.

1. Product overview
Purpose: Provide a consistent, cost-aware inference runtime across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments so engineering teams can ship LLM features with predictable latency, cost, and reliability.
Key user problems solved
- Predictable per-token economics for production LLMs across different hardware and model families.
- Simple API parity across Hosted / Dedicated / Private deployments.
- Operational visibility and automatic graceful degradation (fallbacks, routing policies).

Primary capabilities (v13 scope)
- Unified REST/SDK interface with streaming, function calling, and structured outputs.
- Model routing policies with cost/latency prioritization and automated fallback to compatible quantized variants.
- Redwood Optimize integration: autosuggest batching/quantization profiles and cache hints.
- Enhanced observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-model SLO dashboards, and anomaly alerts tied to evals.

Success metrics (KPIs)
- Hosted API p50 latency for 512-token generation: target <= 320ms (gpu-optimized models).
- Unit inference cost reduction: 15% YoY improvement from batching/cache suggestions.
- Customer adoption: 40% of new enterprise accounts adopt Dedicated within 90 days of sign-up.
- Reliability: 99.95% p95 availability for committed Dedicated capacity.

2. PRD: requirements and acceptance criteria
Scope for v13 (this document focuses on the product-surface and operational requirements delivered in v13):
- Model routing and fallback rules supporting latency-first and cost-first policies across model variants.
- Redwood Optimize automated suggestions surfaced in Console and API for batching/quantization.
- Token-level cost and latency analytics in Console (per-route, per-model).
- Deployment parity guarantees: same API and config semantics across Hosted / Dedicated / Private.
- Rollout controls: canary, A/B, automatic fallback.

User stories (high-level)
- As an app engineer, I want requests to route to a lower-cost quantized variant when latency budget allows, so I reduce my per-token bill without manual tuning.
- As an SRE, I want token-level cost and latency traces per model so I can investigate regressions and tune batching.
- As a platform admin, I want consistent config semantics across Private and Hosted so migrations do not require app changes.

Non-functional requirements
- Latency SLOs: p50/p95 for 32/512 tokens documented per model profile.
- Backwards compatibility: existing API request/response shapes must be honored; new fields optional.
- Security: no plaintext customer data sent to third-party services; KMS integrations supported for Private.
- Observability retention: 90 days for token-level summaries (configurable as add-on).

Acceptance criteria (shippable checklist)
1) Model routing: policy UI + SDK API endpoints exist, unit + e2e tests for fallback behaviors.
2) Optimize suggestions surfaced in Console with actionable opt-in buttons and link-to-release-notes.
3) Console dashboards show token-level cost/latency and expose per-route filters.
4) API compatibility: existing customers experience zero breaking changes in 95% of common request shapes.
5) Documentation: quickstarts, migration guide, and migration CLI snippets published.

3. Design and implementation notes
High-level architecture
- Control plane: policy/rollout engine, model catalog, suggestion engine (Optimize) and observability ingestion.
- Data plane (serving runtime): per-model execution optimized kernel selection, continuous batching, KV prefix cache.
- Smart router: enacts per-request policy (latency-first/cost-first), consults model catalog for compatible fallback variants.
- Console + telemetry: traces, token-level cost attribution, alerts tied to evals.

Design decisions and rationale
- Decision: route by policy at control-plane level and enforce in data plane with lightweight metadata tags. Rationale: minimizes cross-service coordination and provides clear audit trail for fallbacks.
- Decision: expose Optimize suggestions as recommendations (opt-in) rather than auto-applying network-wide changes. Rationale: safety and customer control for quality-sensitive workloads.

Key interfaces and examples
- REST API (new fields) — example request to set routing policy:

POST /api/v1/policies
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "name": "latency-first-512",
  "priority": "latency",
  "max_extra_latency_ms": "50",
  "fallbacks": ["gptx-8q-compat","gptx-16q-compat"]
}

- Example SDK snippet (pseudo-code) to create a policy:

// Python
policy = client.policies.create(name="cost-first-256", priority="cost", budget_tokens_per_minute=10000, fallbacks=["gptx-16q-compat"])

Operational tables and configuration (reference)
- SLO table (example):
| Metric | Target | Measurement window | Owner |
| p50 latency (512 tokens) | <=320ms | trailing 7d | runtime-svc |
| p95 latency (512 tokens) | <=800ms | trailing 7d | runtime-svc |
| Dedicated availability | 99.95% | monthly | infra-sre |
| Token cost variance (per model) | <=20% week-to-week | weekly | finance-product |

- Model compatibility matrix (example rows):
| Model family | Quantized variant | Compatible for fallback | Notes |
| gptx-32 | gptx-16q | yes | high mem, slightly lower quality |
| gptx-16 | gptx-8q | yes | suitable for high-throughput requests |

Migration and backward compatibility
- All new API fields are optional. Servers will default to historical behavior when fields omitted.
- Migration guide (summary steps):
1. Readiness: run "redwood-cli verify-compat" against your integration.
2. Enable policy feature flag in staging and run synthetic traffic.
3. Gradually enable routing policy for 10% -> 50% -> 100% of requests with canary.
4. Observe token-level metrics and evals for quality regressions.

4. Roadmap and themes (next 6 months)
Themes by quarter
- Q2 2026: Improve automated quality-safe quantization rollouts (Optimize v3), multi-region routing policies for geo affinity, and private deployment installer simplification.
- Q3 2026: Predictive autoscaling for Dedicated pools (workload-aware scale), tighter SDK parity for advanced routing APIs, and billing contract SKU alignment.
- Q4 2026: Enterprise features: per-tenant usage caps, extended audit logs (365 days), and on-prem HA installer.

Planned milestones (near-term)
- April 2026: GA of policy UI and SDK parity for routing policies (owners: product/runtime).
- May 2026: Redwood Optimize in-console AB test for automated suggestions (owners: product/optimize).
- June 2026: Billing SKUs and pricing tiers published for Dedicated + Optimize add-on (owners: finance/product).

Dependencies and risks
- Kernel/quantization compatibility across model families (risk: quality regressions). Mitigation: conservative AB tests and integrated eval sets.
- Dedicated capacity autoscaling complexity with heterogeneous hardware. Mitigation: phased rollout with synthetic load tests and canaries.

5. Pricing and packaging notes
Pricing goals: be transparent, usage-aligned, and enable a clear upgrade path from Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private.
Pricing constructs
- Hosted API: per-token pricing (input + output tokens) tiered by model family and quantization level.
- Dedicated: monthly committed capacity (vCPU/GPU hours) + per-token runtime surcharge when bursting beyond committed throughput.
- Optimize add-on: flat monthly fee per-seat plus per-GB telemetry retention charge.

New v13 pricing adjustments (proposal)
- Introduce a "quantized-variant" discount: 20% discount on per-token runtime for qualifying quantized variants when used as fallback in cost-first policies. Rationale: encourages use of lower-cost variants and offsets dedicated hardware costs.
- Dedicated SKUs: add two new mid-tier SKUs optimized for throughput-sensitive customers (high-IO GPUs) with committed monthly tokens and priority routing.

Example pricing table (illustrative)
| Offering | Metric | Price (example) | Notes |
| Hosted (gptx-32) | per-1k input+output tokens | $0.60 | standard model family |
| Hosted (gptx-16q) | per-1k tokens | $0.36 | 40% discount for 16q quantized |
| Dedicated mid-tier | monthly commit (tokens) | $12,000 | includes burst capacity |
| Optimize add-on | per-seat/month | $400 | includes suggestion engine and 90d telemetry |

Sales guidance and packaging rules
- Recommend customers start on Hosted API and adopt Optimize suggestions for quick cost savings.
- For sustained high throughput (>=1B tokens/month) propose Dedicated evaluation with finance+sales for committed-backed pricing.
- Private deployments require enterprise contract; offer migration engineering hours as a professional services SKU.

6. Release notes — v13 (2026-03-04)
Overview
This release consolidates the routing policy surface, Optimize suggestions in Console, and token-level cost analytics. It includes GA policy UI, SDK parity, and billing SKU definitions for upcoming Dedicated SKUs.

Notable features
- Policy engine GA: create latency-first and cost-first policies in Console and via SDK.
- Console: token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency filters.
- Optimize: in-console suggestion cards for batching/quantization with one-click apply for permitted accounts.
- Billing: new quantized-variant discount logic and two Dedicated mid-tier SKUs (alpha).

Fixed issues
- Resolved an issue where fallback decisions were occasionally applied out-of-band, leading to inconsistent logs.
- Fixed a paging bug in the Console traces view when filtering by route.

Migration and rollout plan
- Rollout stages
1) Internal dogfood (Mar 04–Mar 11): product & SRE use feature flags to validate GA workflows.
2) Pilot customers (Mar 12–Apr 01): invite 10 existing Dedicated customers to early migration; collect feedback.
3) Gradual public rollout (Apr 05–Apr 26): open to all Hosted customers with opt-in by default for Optimize suggestions.

Rollout checklist for customer success
- Verify account quota and token billing settings.
- Run "redwood-cli verify-compat" and document any warnings.
- If using Private, schedule migration window (maintenance) and share fallback policy recommendations.

Known limitations
- Some older quantized variants may not support streaming outputs; Console will warn when suggestions are applicable but streaming is unsupported.
- Optimize suggestions currently do not auto-apply for Private installations without admin approval.

Operational runbooks and escalation
- If fallback loops occur (requests repeatedly falling between variants), toggle policy to last-known-good variant and open an incident with "runtime-fallback" tag.
- For latency SLO regression post-rollout, run the profiling playbook: "eng-serving-runtime/profiling-playbook" and escalate to runtime pager if p95 exceeds target for >30m.

Appendices
A. Quick CLI commands
# Verify compatibility
redwood-cli verify-compat --api-key $KEY --host https://api.redwood.example.com
# Create a cost-first policy via CLI
redwood-cli policies create --name cost-first-256 --priority cost --fallbacks gptx-16q-compat
